text:
maria: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection change yesterday we started seeing a subtle perf regression for long-stream requests hitting EU region. Noticed higher token-latency tail and increased cross-region failovers to US-west.
kenji: Ugh. Any recent changes to batching heuristics at the same time?
maria: We changed the kernel scoring to favor quantized kernels for seq_len > 1024; that pushed more requests to a kernel variant that has worse KV cache locality.
san: I have flamegraphs and token-level traces — looks like KV cache misses spike shortly after the new kernel warms up. Token processing time increases ~18% p95 for affected routes.
anya: Can you paste the profiler snippet?
san: Sure — from perf-runner:
```
profile: route=/chat/stream model=redwood-xl-70b quantized=true kernel=attn-opt
token_latency_ms: mean=6.2 p95=18.3 p99=42.1
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.72 -> 0.41 after switch
batch_size_dist: median=4 mean=5.1
```
kenji: kv_cache_hit_rate dropping like that explains the token tail. Do we have per-token latency breakdown in Grafana for these routes?
maria: Not at token granularity per-route+region. We only have aggregate token latency by model and region. This is the core ask: add token-level breakdowns split by route, region, kernel_variant, and batch_size.
anya: Agree — without that we can't tell if it's kernel selection or routing policy causing cross-region fallbacks.
perf-bot: alert: cross_region_failover_rate for eu-central increased from 0.6% to 3.8% (24h)
kenji: The routing policy triggers failover when latency > 200ms for 2 consecutive samples — if token tail increases, more requests trip the threshold and get routed to US-west. That matches timeline.
san: I put together two PromQL queries we can use as a start:
1) per-token-latency by route/region/kernel:
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_processing_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route, region, kernel_variant))
```
2) kv cache hit rate by kernel and region:
```
sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) by(kernel_variant, region) / sum(rate(kv_cache_lookups_total[5m])) by(kernel_variant, region)
```
maria: Nice. Can we also instrument a small counter for routing-decisions with the reason label (latency_threshold, capacity, healthcheck)? We need to know why it fell back.
kenji: I can add `routing_decision_total{reason="latency_threshold"|"capacity"|"model_mismatch"}` in the router. Small patch.
anya: Dashboard plan: add a row for affected routes with panels: token p50/p95/p99, kv hit rate, batch size histogram, routing_decision_total split by reason, cross-region latency map.
perf-bot: suggestion: add alert if kv_cache_hit_rate drops >10% vs baseline for a kernel_variant in a region for 15m.
san: Also, we should record a short perf-snapshot on the host when we flip kernel scoring back to old one to compare. Patch + roll back test.
maria: Who owns the rollout? I can coordinate a rollback if we confirm.
kenji: I'll own the router metric and kernel scoring flag (toggle via feature-flip). Will do a small canary: 5% of traffic in eu-central.
anya: I'll create the Grafana dashboard (starter panels + templating for route/region/kernel) and add links in the incident board.
sam: Can we schedule a quick sync — 30m — to triage and decide rollback? I'm available in 15.
maria: Meeting in 15. Agenda: confirm instrumentation, deploy router metric, run canary, decide rollback.
ops-bot: deploybot: canary rollout queued: kenji/kernel-router-metrics at 10:15 UTC
kenji: starting with metrics-only deploy (no behavioral change). If we see kv hit-rate drop on the metrics-only rollout then kernel scoring is likely the culprit.
maria: Thanks. Please post the dashboard link and the canary results into this thread.
kenji: will do.
anya: leaving a TODO: add per-token heatmap panel (x axis token index, y axis p95 latency) + region selector. That will make regression hunting faster.
perf-bot: note: when adding heatmaps keep memory cost in mind — use 1m rollups.
maria: quick reminder: tag owners with @ in dashboard so alerts route to the right oncall.
kenji: ack. updating the patch now.
sam: cheers, see you in the sync.
